title: Linear regression
tagline: Find the line that minimizes squared error between predictions and truth.
history: Least squares was published by Legendre (1805) and Gauss (~1809); Galton coined "regression" in the 1880s while studying regression to the mean.
useCases: Estimating the effect size of a feature
whenToUse: A roughly linear relationship when you want interpretable coefficients.
whenNotToUse: Strong non-linearity, heavy multicollinearity (add Ridge/Lasso), or non-constant noise.
complexity: Closed form O(n·d² + d³) · gradient descent O(n·d·i)
note: Same machinery as gradient descent. Here the descent tunes two parameters — slope and intercept — and you watch the line snap onto the points.

code.python:
import numpy as np

def linear_regression(X, y):
    # closed form: w = (XᵀX)⁻¹ Xᵀy, with a bias column
    Xb = np.c_[np.ones(len(X)), X]
    return np.linalg.pinv(Xb.T @ Xb) @ Xb.T @ y   # [bias, slope...]
code.ruby:
def linear_regression(xs, ys)
  n  = xs.size.to_f
  mx = xs.sum / n
  my = ys.sum / n
  slope = xs.zip(ys).sum { |x, y| (x - mx) * (y - my) } /
          xs.sum { |x| (x - mx) ** 2 }
  [my - slope * mx, slope]   # [intercept, slope]
end
